Patients with pulmonary hypertension have raised plasma concentrations of the potent vasoconstrictor endothelin I, and endothelin antag- onists such as bosentan have therefore been tried. Studies1,2 with oral bosentan have shown improvement in exercise tolerance and in time to clinical progression; an open study3 showed sus- tained benefit with treatment for 1 year or more. However, no effect on mortality has yet been found in randomised studies, al- though there is some evidence4,5 that survival may be improved. Bosentan has also been tried with epoprostenol.6 There was a non-significant trend towards greater improvement in the group receiving both drugs compared with epoprostenol alone. There is some evidence that bosentan may be of benefit in pul- monary hypertension associated with congenital heart disease,7,8 including Eisenmenger syndrome,8-10 and in pulmonary hyper- tension associated with HIV infection.11 Positive results have also been reported12-14 in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. 1.
